subject.title: Cloud-worker reclaim drops worker-authored Git commits

question: Should this be scheduled as the full Git-mode reconciliation/recovery repair now, rather than a file-only reclaim patch?
rationale: The documented contract establishes commit adoption, but the fix spans Git object transfer, ancestry verification, compare-and-swap ownership, durable recovery, and live cloud-worker proof; maintainers need to set the delivery boundary before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor full reconciliation repair
options.body: Implement verified commit import, managed-worktree fast-forward, durable HEAD/index recovery, focused fault tests, and a live cloud-worker proof.

options.title: Track as milestone work
options.body: Keep the documented contract and record the observed regression, but defer implementation until the broader reconciliation/checkpoint milestone is actively staffed.

recommendation.title: Sponsor full reconciliation repair
recommendation.body: Implement verified commit import, managed-worktree fast-forward, durable HEAD/index recovery, focused fault tests, and a live cloud-worker proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The report and the referenced cloud-worker design establish the relevant behavior and the required Gateway-versus-worker ownership boundary.
